title: Bobby Stark and Chick Webb's rehearsing band
summary: Bobby Stark was his favorite hard-driving trumpeter; Webb loved rehearsing, hired only the best, and nearly had Ellington in his band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: But now, you liked Bobby Stark.

Oh, Bobby! Yeah, that's my man. He could blow. Nice trumpet player. Good man in a band. Good man in a band. Yeah. Chick had eight pieces, an eight-piece band, you know. There was Bobby Stark... I'm trying to think. He had... There was four in the rhythm, right?

And there was Johnny, Elmer Williams on tenor, Bobby Stark on... Yeah, two brass. Bobby and Slats on trombone. I was thinking that Chick had another trumpet, but he didn't have another trumpet until I went in the band, and I worked with Chick... Which wasn't long, because he didn't work much. I think we had a ten-day engagement up in New England, ten one-nighters, you know. And I worked them with him. That's when he was enlarging his band. And when

we came back, he didn't have no more work! But we was rehearsing every day. He loved to rehearse, he loved to hear his band, and stand on the corner and talk about how great a band he has. And he'd tell you about all the men in the band, this-that-and-the-other... He didn't have nothin' but the best men.
Did he have Jimmy Harrison at one time?

He had everybody. He had everybody. He damn near had Duke Ellington! Well, he could have got Duke, too, because Duke wasn't doin' nothin'. Duke wasn't doin' nothin' but standing at a bar waiting for a live one to come in. And Duke, he went to work... Duke went to work for Billy Cain's club on Eighth Avenue, a little joint, you know. Then after that, Duke left town and went up to New England, barnstorming through New England. They stayed up there all summer. When they come back from that, then they went in the Cotton Club. Then from then on, he didn't look back. So he almost had Duke in his band.

But Chick would hire anybody quick. You had to be good. Chick didn't want nothin' but the best. And he would tell everybody that he had the best, too. That's what he would tell you. And he spent his money buying arrangements. He'd get good arrangements, and he'd get good men that could play the arrangements. And he had a good-sounding band. It
sounded very good. I'm not talking about the time I was with him, because I made them ten days, and we just rehearsed from then on. He didn't get no more engagements.
